post_title: gpu  is not used in simulation only cpu
post_details: HI, maybe I miss something , I am starting with some basic stuff ,just creating a basic t-shirt and I try to simulate with GPU, but I check it and CPU is used instead of cpu. I have a RTX 3060 and AMD 7700x. some hints? thanks

comments.comment_body: You are likely experiencing this issue because Marvelous Designer does not support AMD graphics cards for GPU simulation: see the manual link here https://marvelousdesigner.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/9848688288665-System-Requirements LUCKILY you want to be working in CPU for your workflow anyway. GPU simulation is inaccurate and has inaccurate simulation. Here is the workflow order from our discord channel and invite here https://discord.gg/HAh568h Workflows for simulation in ORDER: 1. GPU - use at start if necessary. Best for large amounts of fabric. Not good for accuracy, not meant for anything other than settling large amounts of cloth into the scene at FIRST. WILL have collision issues, not accurate cloth sim. PLEASE DO NOT KEEP WORKING IN GPU you will encounter inaccuracies and "bugs" 2. CPU - Recommended use: Majority of workflow. What you want to work in until the end for final simulation, can also be the final simulation stage depending on workflow. Accurate cloth simulation, most recommended simulation option. Used in all official tutorials unless stated otherwise 3. Accurate Fabric -Use at end if necessary: slowest, most accurate for real life simulation, used to remove skin offset &amp additional collision thickness (may not in V12)

post_title: Import avatar(.fbx) and apply texture

post_description: This web page provides guidance on separating dress meshes and applying textures to imported avatar files in Marvelous Designer 12.

comments.comment_body: Thank you for contacting us, First of all, you need to import your garment and character separately. You need to import your character mesh as "Avatar" for "Object Type" during import. And for garment file, you would need to use .OBJ file format and chose "Garment" for "Object Type". If you import your garment using OBJ, you can simulate but the parameters you can adjust is limited. You would not able to assign fabric to it. However, Marvelous Designer does not have a render engine build inside. The textures for the fabrics in Marvelous designer are also built with diffuse and normal maps. You are still able to use it in the render engine you are using. You can also check the "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map" option during your .OBJ import if you have proper UV for your mesh. By checking this, Marvelous Designer will create pattern pieces base on your UV shell. Patterns will show up in the 2D window, and you will be able to use all of the functions in Marvelous Designer. This might be best method for you. For tutorial on "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map", please watch this tutorial here [LINK] I would strongly recommend you to watch our Quick Start tutorials to learn the basics in using Marvelous Designer, you can find these tutorials here [LINK] I also recommend you to join our discord channel, you would get faster respond from you peer here. [Discord Invite Link] Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

Hi Lai Edgar, Thank you for contacting us, The reason why this is happening is because your character scale is too small. The default unit in Marvelous designer is millimeter, and your character is currently only around 20 millimeters tall. When import your character, you can set the import scale, please make sure your character is at a similar size as the avatars in the Marvelous Designer library. You are able to change the subdivision of the mesh using the particle distance setting in the property editor. a lower particle distance will make the mesh denser. randomized triangle will produced the most realist cloth quality in simulation, since the mesh can only be bend along the edges of the geometry. So when you import your .OBJ and checked "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map", Marvelous designer will recreate your garment by tracing your mesh UV. If you want to simulate with your original remeshed geometry, please uncheck "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map" but still import it as a garment. Please note that, by unchecking "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map", you are able to simulate, but the amount of parameters and properties you are able to adjust is limited. Please watch our Quick start Tutorials for more information on the above subjects [Link] Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

comments.comment_body: Hi Lina, Thank you for contacting us, Both options only affect the location where the texture images are saved, it would have noting to do with your Geometry file (.OBJ). If you chose Absolute Texture Image File Path (which is by default), Marvelous Designer will save the texture files related to your geometry into the same location with your .OBJ file. And "Save With Texture Files (.zip)" Exports the .OBJ file, .MTL file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file. In both case you can import your .OBJ directly into Blender, and you would need to build the shader your self inside Blender. The shader you use depends on the render engine you are using. Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

comments.comment_body: Hi, Thank you for contacting us, It is most likely because all of your pattern pieces have solidify applied. If you select your pattern pieces, go to the property editor and check if this check box is being checked. In Marvelous Designer, when you apply 3D statement like strengthen, freeze, bind and solidify, the color will change in the 3D window to indicate where these properties are being applied. It is very unlikely that the whole garment need to be solidified. Please check this tutorial video to learn more about the different 3D statements and what they do: [LINK] Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team
